input.strategy_title: Make RHOAI more usable for enterprise teams
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Several strategic accounts have told field teams that RHOAI "feels hard to use
at enterprise scale". Feedback arrived through different channels and has not
been consolidated; the quotes below are representative but partially
contradictory. Leadership wants visible usability progress this release.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | — | Administration should be simpler. One account wants fewer configuration options exposed ("too many knobs"), another explicitly wants more fine-grained controls per project. |
| HLR-2 | — | Onboarding a new data scientist should take "less than a day". It is not defined what onboarding includes or where the day is currently spent. |
| HLR-3 | — | The platform should "integrate better" with existing enterprise tooling. No specific tools were named in the consolidated feedback. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Publish a whitepaper describing enterprise usability best practices on RHOAI. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks

## Out of Scope

Nothing has been explicitly scoped out.

## Open Questions

1. Which accounts' feedback takes precedence when requirements conflict (HLR-1)?
2. What does "onboarding" cover for HLR-2 — cluster access, project setup,
   first workbench, or first deployed model?
3. Which enterprise tools does HLR-3 actually mean?

# Implement simplified enterprise admin configuration experience

## Description

Conditional branch: exists only if the enterprise admin configuration UX
direction resolves in favor of simplification (fewer configuration options
exposed). Delivers a streamlined administrative experience in the RHOAI
Dashboard: fewer exposed configuration options for enterprise administrators,
backed by curated defaults, per the enumerated scope of the direction
decision.

## Scope

- Reduce the number of configuration options exposed to administrators in
  the Dashboard admin experience, per the enumerated scope from the direction
  decision.
- Provide curated defaults for the no-longer-exposed options so streamlined
  deployments behave correctly without manual tuning.
- Keep prior behavior recoverable for administrators who relied on the
  previously exposed options, per the rollback/feature-flag requirement for
  work that replaces an existing capability surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The number of exposed admin configuration options is reduced per the
  direction decision's enumerated scope; each removed option has a documented
  curated default.
- Streamlined deployments behave correctly with the curated defaults for the
  covered scenarios.
- The change ships behind a feature flag or equivalent rollback mechanism;
  reverting restores the previously exposed configuration surface.
- Existing Dashboard functionality outside the admin configuration surface
  is unaffected (regression suite passes).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (administration should be simpler; "too many knobs" feedback) — this
  branch delivers the simplification outcome when that direction is selected.

# Implement fine-grained per-project administrative controls

## Description

Conditional branch: exists only if the enterprise admin configuration UX
direction resolves in favor of granularity (more fine-grained controls per
project). Delivers per-project administrative controls in the RHOAI Dashboard,
layered on the existing platform-wide settings, per the enumerated scope of
the direction decision.

## Scope

- Add per-project administrative control capability to the Dashboard admin
  experience, per the enumerated scope from the direction decision.
- Layer per-project controls on top of existing platform-wide settings:
  platform-wide values remain the default where no per-project override is
  set.
- Keep the change reversible for administrators, per the rollback /
  feature-flag requirement for work that reshapes an existing capability
  surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Administrators can configure the enumerated controls at per-project
  granularity through the Dashboard.
- Projects without explicit overrides inherit the existing platform-wide
  behavior unchanged.
- The change ships behind a feature flag or equivalent rollback mechanism;
  reverting restores the prior platform-wide-only configuration behavior.
- Existing Dashboard functionality outside the admin configuration surface
  is unaffected (regression suite passes).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (administration should be simpler; account asking for fine-grained
  per-project controls) — this branch delivers the granularity outcome when
  that direction is selected.

# Resolve enterprise admin configuration UX direction (simplification vs. fine-grained controls)

## Description

Enterprise feedback on administration is contradictory: one strategic account
wants fewer configuration options exposed ("too many knobs"), while another
explicitly wants more fine-grained controls per project. The feedback arrived
through different channels and has not been consolidated. This investigation
consolidates that feedback, determines which direction takes precedence for
the RHOAI admin configuration experience (or whether a blended approach is
viable), and produces a decision record that determines which implementation
work is executed.

## Scope

- Consolidate all field/account feedback channels contributing to the
  admin-usability complaints into a single inventory with attributed use
  cases.
- Identify the conflicting accounts and characterize the workflows behind
  each ask (operator vs. project-admin vs. end-user perspective).
- Evaluate the candidate directions against the existing Dashboard admin
  configuration model (settings administered through the Dashboard
  configuration CR and surfaced in the console).
- Produce a decision record selecting one of: (a) simplify the exposed
  configuration with curated defaults, (b) add fine-grained per-project
  administrative controls, or (c) a blended approach.
- Enumerate the resulting implementation scope (which admin configuration
  surfaces change under the selected direction).

## Acceptance Criteria

- All feedback channels contributing to the "too many knobs" vs.
  "fine-grained controls" conflict are consolidated into a single inventory
  with attributed use cases — no known channel is left unconsolidated.
- A documented decision selects one direction (or a justified blend), with
  rationale tied to account impact and measured against the platform's
  existing admin configuration surfaces.
- The implementation scope for the selected direction is enumerated
  (configuration surfaces affected, expected user-visible change), sufficient
  to start implementation without a further discovery step.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (administration should be simpler; conflicting account feedback) —
  this investigation resolves the open question of which feedback takes
  precedence; the resulting implementation work is selected conditionally on
  the outcome.

# Define data-scientist onboarding scope and baseline first-day time breakdown

## Description

The strategy requires that onboarding a new data scientist take "less than a
day", but it is not defined what onboarding includes (cluster access, project
setup, first workbench, or first deployed model) or where the day is currently
spent. This investigation defines the onboarding boundary, measures the
current-state baseline, and produces a ranked list of friction points — the
deliverables that determine what onboarding-improvement work is built and
where it targets.

## Scope

- Define the onboarding journey boundary for a new data scientist: which
  stages are in scope (account/cluster access, project setup, first workbench
  spawn, first deployed model) and which are explicitly out of scope.
- Measure where a new data scientist's first day is currently spent, per
  stage, producing a baseline time breakdown.
- Identify and rank the dominant friction points in the in-scope stages
  (e.g., workbench provisioning wait time, configuration discovery,
  permissions hurdles), based on the measured baseline.
- Produce a measurable onboarding target statement consistent with the
  "less than a day" requirement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The onboarding definition enumerates the stages in and out of scope, with
  rationale, and is agreed with product stakeholders.
- A baseline time breakdown per in-scope stage exists, measured on a
  representative cluster configuration rather than estimated.
- The top friction points are identified and ranked by contribution to total
  onboarding time, with enough detail to scope remediation work.
- The "less than a day" target is restated as a measurable criterion against
  the defined scope (which stages it covers and how it is measured).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (onboarding a new data scientist should take less than a day) — this
  investigation resolves the open questions of what onboarding covers and
  where the day is currently spent; downstream implementation scope is
  determined by its outcome.

# Identify target enterprise tooling for RHOAI integration

## Description

The strategy asks that the platform "integrate better" with existing
enterprise tooling, but no specific tools were named in the consolidated
feedback. This investigation determines which enterprise tools the strategic
accounts actually mean, validates the demand, and produces a prioritized
shortlist with a mapping of where each integration would land in the platform
— the deliverable that determines whether integration work exists and what it
targets.

## Scope

- Consolidate which enterprise tools the strategic accounts and field teams
  refer to (e.g., identity providers, source control, ticketing, monitoring,
  data platforms), with the originating account attributed.
- Validate demand per candidate tool (how many accounts, what workflow the
  integration unblocks).
- Assess feasibility per candidate: which platform surface the integration
  would touch (console experience, authentication, workbench environment,
  serving/pipeline integrations) and any upstream or vendor coordination it
  requires.
- Produce a prioritized integration shortlist with recommended integration
  surface and rough effort per entry, sufficient to scope implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A candidate tool list exists with attributed demand per strategic account —
  no known feedback channel is left unconsolidated.
- Each shortlisted tool has a mapped integration surface in the platform and
  a stated feasibility assessment (including any upstream/vendor dependency).
- A prioritized shortlist with a documented ranking rationale is produced and
  agreed with product stakeholders.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (the platform should integrate better with existing enterprise
  tooling) — this investigation resolves the open question of which tools are
  actually meant; downstream integration work is gated on its outcome.

# Reduce data-scientist onboarding time to under one day

## Description

Implements the onboarding improvements that bring a new data scientist's
first day under the one-day target, targeting the friction points identified
by the onboarding-scope definition and baseline work. The concrete scope of
this epic (which stages and surfaces change) is determined by that
investigation's outcome; this epic cannot start until the onboarding
definition and baseline exist.

## Scope

- Reduce friction in the onboarding stages the onboarding definition
  identified as the dominant first-day cost — within the Workbenches/Notebooks
  surface (workbench spawn flow, defaults, provisioning behavior, idle
  handling) and, where the baseline points there, coordinated changes to the
  console surfaces a new data scientist traverses.
- Address the top-ranked friction points from the baseline breakdown; defer
  lower-ranked ones explicitly with rationale.
- Verify the improvement against the measured baseline, using the measurable
  onboarding target produced by the onboarding definition work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Onboarding time for a new data scientist, measured across the defined
  onboarding scope and with the same measurement method as the baseline, is
  under one day.
- The top-ranked friction points from the baseline breakdown are addressed,
  or explicitly deferred with documented rationale.
- Changes preserve existing workbench lifecycle behavior for current users;
  any change to default behavior is reversible (configuration default or
  feature flag) so administrators can restore prior behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (onboarding a new data scientist should take less than a day) — this
  epic delivers the measurable onboarding-time reduction once the scope and
  baseline are defined.

# Integrate RHOAI with prioritized enterprise tooling

## Description

Implements the enterprise tooling integrations selected by the tooling
identification work, so that RHOAI fits the toolchains the strategic accounts
already run. The concrete scope of this epic (which tools, which integration
surfaces) is determined by that investigation's prioritized shortlist; this
epic cannot start until the shortlist exists.

## Scope

- Implement the integrations on the prioritized shortlist, on the platform
  surfaces the identification work mapped for each tool (console experience,
  authentication, workbench environment, or serving/pipeline integration as
  determined).
- Coordinate any upstream or vendor dependency the identification work
  flagged for a shortlisted integration.
- Validate each integration against the enterprise environment expectations
  defined during tooling identification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each shortlisted integration is implemented on its mapped platform surface
  and demonstrably works with the corresponding enterprise tool.
- Integrations requiring upstream or vendor coordination track that
  dependency explicitly, with a stated fallback if it stalls.
- Integrations are reversible or additive: existing platform behavior for
  users who do not use the integrated tooling is unchanged.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (the platform should integrate better with existing enterprise
  tooling) — this epic delivers the concrete integrations once the target
  tools are identified and prioritized.

# Publish enterprise usability best-practices whitepaper

## Description

Authors and publishes, through the Red Hat docs content process, a whitepaper
describing enterprise usability best practices on RHOAI. The whitepaper
consolidates the usability outcomes of this strategy — the resolved
enterprise admin configuration direction, the onboarding improvements, and
the enterprise tooling integrations — into prescriptive guidance for
enterprise teams adopting RHOAI.

## Scope

- Produce a content outline covering: enterprise admin configuration
  practices (per the resolved direction), recommended data-scientist
  onboarding paths (per the defined onboarding scope and measured
  improvements), and enterprise tooling integration guidance (per the
  delivered integrations).
- Author the whitepaper using the Red Hat docs content tooling and process.
- Have the content technically reviewed against the implemented outcomes
  before publication.
- Publish the whitepaper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The whitepaper is published and covers enterprise usability best practices
  for admin configuration, onboarding, and enterprise tooling integration on
  RHOAI.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implemented platform behavior
  (admin configuration direction as delivered, measured onboarding
  improvements, delivered tooling integrations) — reviewed by someone with
  knowledge of the implementations, with review comments resolved.
- Guidance reflects the actually-selected admin configuration direction and
  the measured onboarding results, not the pre-decision contradictory
  feedback.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (publish a whitepaper describing enterprise usability best practices
  on RHOAI) — this epic delivers the whitepaper.
